gen_risks.description: Construction may not be completed before winter, causing seasonal delays and extending the project timeline.
gen_risks.mitigation: Advance procurement, pre‑fabrication of components, and a detailed construction schedule that secures critical activities early in the season with contingency time.
gen_risks.evidence: If it cannot be completed before winter, the Project will have more delays with waiting for the next construction season.

gen_risks.description: Absence of local manufacturers for 220 kV poles and conductors forces reliance on imports, risking delays and cost increases.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure early contracts with qualified foreign suppliers, include delivery buffers, and explore regional sourcing options with price escalation clauses.
gen_risks.evidence: there is no local company who can produce metal poles and conductors meeting the standards for 220kV lines.

gen_risks.description: Perceived high corruption and interference by senior officials could stall procurement processes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use the e‑GP portal for transparent bidding, independent evaluation committees, and strict adherence to World Bank procurement rules with external monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: High level of corruption perception.

gen_risks.description: Election‑driven changes in government officials may disrupt project continuity and decision‑making.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalize hand‑over protocols, maintain institutional memory through the Project Steering Committee, and brief incoming officials promptly.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential changes in Government officials involved in project activities due to election cycle... H

gen_risks.description: The Project Management Office (PMO) is not yet established and staff lack experience with Bank procedures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit a qualified financial officer immediately, provide intensive Bank‑led training, and use an Owner’s Engineer to fill expertise gaps.
gen_risks.evidence: Readiness of the Project’s financial management arrangements: A PMO is not yet established and a qualified financial officer... S

gen_risks.description: Weak internal controls could lead to misallocation of loan funds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and approve a detailed Financial Management Manual with segregation of duties, regular internal audits, and Bank oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: Weak internal controls... H

gen_risks.description: Poor budgeting may result in funds being spent on non‑intended purposes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare annual budgets approved by the PSC, conduct quarterly variance analyses, and enforce corrective actions for deviations.
gen_risks.evidence: Poor budgeting: The project funds not used for the intended purposes... H

gen_risks.description: Selected accounting software may be unreliable, compromising financial reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Choose proven commercial software, pilot test before rollout, and maintain manual records for the first three months as a backup.
gen_risks.evidence: Reliability of the accounting system... S

gen_risks.description: Complex Treasury arrangements could cause bottlenecks in fund disbursement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a zero‑balance account, define clear SOPs, and ensure close coordination between MOF and MOE for cash‑flow monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: Delays and bottlenecks in the project funds flow arrangements... H

gen_risks.description: Seasonal nature of civil works may lead to construction delays if the season ends before completion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Advance procurement of materials, schedule critical activities early, and use modular construction techniques to accelerate progress.
gen_risks.evidence: seasonal nature of civil works in Mongolia adds more risks to the Project.

gen_risks.description: Heavy reliance on imported construction materials (75‑80%) exposes the project to pandemic or border‑closure disruptions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Identify alternative regional suppliers, maintain buffer stocks, and include force‑majeure clauses in supply contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: construction sector ... 75-80% of construction materials are sourced from outside the country... pandemic or border closures could have a significant impact.

gen_risks.description: Local construction materials have shown quality deficiencies (40% unqualified), risking substandard works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strict pre‑qualification, independent testing of materials, and use rated criteria that include quality as a non‑price factor.
gen_risks.evidence: 40% of construction materials were found unqualified in the local market.

gen_risks.description: Transmission line construction and operation pose bird collision and biodiversity impacts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply the Bird Management Plan, install flight diverters, and monitor avian activity throughout construction and operation.
gen_risks.evidence: Construction of new transmission lines... bird collision risk... BMP addresses and manages the potential impacts of the transmission line on avifauna biodiversity.

gen_risks.description: Workers and nearby communities may be exposed to electromagnetic fields (EMF) and other OHS hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Follow EHSG guidelines, enforce safe distances, provide PPE and training, and conduct regular EMF monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: During operation and maintenance phases... exposure to EMF, workers health and OHS including risk of electrocutions.

gen_risks.description: Extreme climate events (flooding, wildfires, landslides) could damage the transmission infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design towers to withstand high wind, snow, earthquake, and flood loads; route through low‑risk terrain; incorporate climate‑resilient standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Mongolia is prone to risks from climate hazards such as flooding, wildfires, and landslides... moderate risk... enhanced engineering and design standards.

gen_risks.description: Construction activities may restrict herders' access to pasture and increase traffic, causing community dissatisfaction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a community liaison plan, schedule works to minimize access loss, implement traffic‑management measures, and provide temporary compensation where needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Community safety during the construction phase, with temporary restriction of access to resources by local herders... traffic increase.

gen_risks.description: Ineffective grievance redress mechanism could lead to escalated complaints and project delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the two‑stage GRM, train staff on resolution procedures, and monitor resolution timelines to ensure timely outcomes.
gen_risks.evidence: The project level grievance redress mechanism (GRM) will replicate the mechanisms... two‑stage approach.

gen_risks.description: Gender imbalance in the National Power Transmission Grid workforce may hinder achievement of gender targets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a gender gap assessment, introduce gender‑responsive HR policies, and monitor women’s share in technical and managerial roles.
gen_risks.evidence: Women represent 28.8 percent of the total workforce... low representation in senior positions.

gen_risks.description: Private investors may not develop the expected 100 MW of VRE, limiting the project's renewable integration goals.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide additional de‑risking tools such as guarantees, facilitate power purchase agreements, and conduct market outreach to attract investors.
gen_risks.evidence: Given the current enabling environment... only 100 MW will be developed by private investors.

gen_risks.description: Current electricity tariffs are below cost, risking utility financial deficits that could affect payment for transmission services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Support the government’s tariff reform study, design cost‑recovery mechanisms, and implement phased tariff adjustments aligned with regulatory approval.
gen_risks.evidence: current electricity price is below the cost of service... financial deficit could reach 36 percent of system costs by end of 2025.

gen_risks.description: High existing transmission losses (13.4%) and poor reliability may reduce the net benefits of the new line.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use low‑loss conductors, optimize line routing, and conduct post‑commissioning loss audits to ensure performance targets are met.
gen_risks.evidence: combined transmission and distribution losses in CES in 2021 remained high at 13.4 percent... SAIDI 16 days.

gen_risks.description: CAPEX overruns could erode the project’s economic rate of return.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include a contingency reserve, adopt fixed‑price contracts where feasible, and monitor costs against the baseline monthly.
gen_risks.evidence: Sensitivity analysis shows project ERR robust... cost overrun considered.

gen_risks.description: Local contractors lack sufficient human resources and evaluation committees lack English expertise, risking procurement delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted training for contractors and evaluation committee members, and use bilingual procurement documents with Bank support.
gen_risks.evidence: many local companies lack human resources... Evaluation Committee members normally do not have knowledge and experience in handling English documents.

gen_risks.description: Interference by high‑level officials in procurement decisions may cause procedural delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a clear procurement manual with delegated authority, and enforce oversight by the PSC and independent monitors.
gen_risks.evidence: Frequent change of the decision‑making officials for the Project. Interference of the high‑level officials in procurement decision making which leads to delays.

gen_risks.description: Non‑compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework could trigger project suspension.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a robust ESMP, conduct regular compliance audits, and provide continuous E&S capacity building for MOE staff.
gen_risks.evidence: MOE is familiar with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and has a satisfactory track record... capacity building identified.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risks are rated Substantial. The parliamentary election was held in June 2024 and a new coalition government was formed, with representation of all three major political parties. While there may be risks of disagreement on the approval of individual projects, these risks will be mitigated by the strong alignment of the proposed operation with the NRP and the new Government Action Plan for 2024-2028.
gt_risks.mitigation: Continued engagement with key stakeholders, including government and the parliament, through ongoing analytical and technical support on VRE integration and energy sector reform, will help mitigate risks going forward. The Development Partner Group, co-chaired by the World Bank and UNDP, will also offer a donor coordination platform to maintain political momentum for RE integration.

gt_risks.description: The macroeconomic risk is rated Substantial. Mongolia's economic outlook is dependent on global macroeconomic factors, in particular commodity prices. Despite recent positive short-term developments from coal and agricultural exports, Mongolia still needs to strengthen fiscal and external buffers to respond to future shocks and continue reforms aimed at diversifying the economy.
gt_risks.mitigation: To mitigate these risks and manage external balances, the World Bank has been, and will continue to be, supporting the authorities in restoring fiscal and external buffers through analytical and advisory work.

gt_risks.description: The sector strategies and policies risk is rated Substantial. Substantial risk still exists due to institutional fragmentation, lack of policies to promote RE projects, and lack of clear commitment of reforms, especially related to tariff reforms that are crucial to make the sector viable and be able to refinance projects.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigation measures include actively engaging in multi-stakeholder coordination meetings and providing technical advice and capacity building to key stakeholders.

gt_risks.description: The institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk is rated Substantial. The implementing agency MOE and NPTG have experience implementing World Bank-funded projects; however, there is a substantial risk that newly hired PMO staff may not have sufficient capacity, which could potentially lead to implementation delays.
gt_risks.mitigation: The PMO will be strengthened with experienced consultants and targeted training and capacity building. Mitigating measures include the World Bank's scrutiny of PMO members' selection, including a review of the TOR and providing no objection to the qualification criteria of the staff.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. There are substantial risks due to the reliance of MOE on a newly constituted PMO, which may cause delays in processing payments, conducting IFRs, and other reporting requirements; the construction sector in Mongolia is often subject to delays and cost overruns. Potential procurement risks include (i) likelihood of time and cost overruns due to weak contract management capacity, and (ii) significant procurement delays due to delayed initiation of procurement and establishment of needed staffing arrangements.
gt_risks.mitigation: Capacity building through customized training and TA is a central element of the Project, along with strong project supervision and contract management capacity building; MOE will continue to directly provide intensive support to the PMO. Procurement risks are mitigated by (a) establishing a PMO with appropriate procurement and technical staff per FIDIC contract standards; (b) clearly defined workflow in decision-making within the MOE/PMO procurement manual; and (c) extensive market engagement to stimulate market participation.
